properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 2:56AM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:

Islip, moving northeast at 30 mph.

unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Shirley, Medford, Manorville, Patchogue, Middle Island, Wading River,
Center Moriches, Coram, Holbrook, Sayville, Farmingville, Mastic,
Rocky Point, Mastic Beach, and Calverton.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued October 12 at 2:38AM EDT until October 12 at 5:45AM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
FFWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Delaware County in southeastern Pennsylvania...
Southern Philadelphia County in southeastern Pennsylvania...

* Until 545 AM EDT.

* At 238 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Philadelphia, Yeadon, Folcroft, Swarthmore, East Lansdowne, South
Philadelphia, Roxborough, Morris Park, Center City, Darby Township,
Philadelphia International Airport and Kensington.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 476 in Pennsylvania between mile markers 6 and 7.
Interstate 76 in Pennsylvania between mile markers 340 and 351.
Interstate 95 in Pennsylvania between mile markers 8 and 30.
Interstate 676 in Pennsylvania between mile markers 0 and 1.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued October 12 at 2:11AM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...

Sandy Hook NJ to Montauk Point out 60 NM...
Long Island South Shore Bays...

At 210 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots. These thunderstorms were
located across several areas extending from 6 nm east of Entrance to
New York Harbor to 54 nm south of The Coastal Waters Southeast Of
Block Island, moving northeast at 30 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Great South Bay, Shinnecock Bay, Buoy 44017, Buoy 44025, Westhampton
Beach, Moriches Inlet, Shinnecock Inlet, Moriches Bay, Montauk Shoal,
and Montauk Point.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until these storms pass.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

French Broad River At at Grove Bridge Rd in Blantyre affecting
Henderson and Transylvania Counties.

rainfall will maintain flooding along the French Broad River.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...French Broad River at Grove Bridge Rd in Blantyre.

* WHEN...Until late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Minor Flooding continues.  Floodwaters

the old  railroad bed. Floodwaters may start to inundate the
shoulders of River Road near the Big Willow Road intersection.

Rd. and Crab Creek Rd. At 18.0 feet, Minor Flooding continues.

old railroad bed is ongoing.  The river may be overtopping the old
railroad bed near Fodderstack Mountain Rd. and River Ridge Rd.  The
intersection of River Rd. and Big Willow Rd. is inundated with
several inches of water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 17.7 feet and slowly rising.
- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:30 PM EDT Sunday was 17.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.8 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 01/03/1937.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Louisiana...Texas...

Calcasieu River near White Oak Park affecting Calcasieu Parish.

Calcasieu River Near Salt Water Barrier affecting Calcasieu Parish.

Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier affecting Jefferson,
Hardin, Orange and Jasper Counties.

For the Calcasieu River...including Glenmora, Oakdale, Oberlin,
Kinder, White Oak Park, Salt Water Barrier...Minor flooding is
forecast.
For the Neches River...including Town Bluff, Evadale, Neches River
Saltwater Barrier...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.0 feet, Water is about two feet over portions of
Four Oaks Ranch Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight and oscillate around flood stage for the
next several days.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 5:41PM EDT until October 12 at 6:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive runoff continues.

* WHERE...Central Henderson County in western North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding around greater Hendersonville.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 535 PM EDT, Mud and Bat Fork Creeks remained in flood and
flooding will continue all afternoon.  The Mud Creek river gage
on North Main Street was nearing 16 feet which indicates flooding
of portions of William H King Memorial Park and the Oklawaha
Greenway.  The river has crested in Hendersonville, but will not
fall below flood stage until late evening or overnight tonight.

- Please obey all barricades and heed all evacuation orders from
local Emergency Management officials.  Only a few inches of water
can strand your vehicle and only 6 inches of water can sweep your
vehicle away.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hendersonville, Fletcher, Flat Rock, Mountain Home, Laurel Park,
Valley Hill and East Flat Rock.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction: Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 2:37PM EDT until October 12 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Alexander County in the piedmont of North
Carolina...
North Central Catawba County in the piedmont of North Carolina...
West Central Iredell County in the piedmont of North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 200 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 228 PM EDT, Catawba River levels continued to rise with the
possibility of Lookout Shoals Lake exceeding 104 feet by this
evening, leading to significant inundation of low-lying areas,
which includes yards, docks and boat launch areas. Vulnerable
properties in the Carpenters Cove community or any other
shoreline interests who would be affected by the high lake
levels, should protect their properties and follow guidance from
Catawba County Emergency Management.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction: Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.
